hypotheses.statement: For the three currently ambiguous legacy G9 rule lines, automatic source-to-IR normalization before an authoritative semantic freeze is unsafe; after explicit freeze, registry-gated typed n-ary PredicateIR/ConstraintIR can preserve deterministic semantic identity.
hypotheses.observation: Each line admitted at least two materially distinct plausible AST hashes; explicit frozen test candidates validated 3/3 and remained hash-stable under 10000 whitespace mutations.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: A grammar precedence/associativity rule alone can uniquely recover the intended semantics of all three lines.
hypotheses.falsifier: Authoritative prior IR/parser evidence or a production parser contract uniquely identifies one intended AST for each line without additional semantic choice.

hypotheses.statement: A relation-signature registry with fixed arity provides a safer BASE boundary than accepting arbitrary bare identifiers as semantic relations.
hypotheses.observation: 10000/10000 unknown-relation mutations and 10000/10000 wrong-arity mutations were rejected fail-closed by the tested registry.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Fail-open arbitrary relation parsing plus later type checking provides equal mutation rejection and diagnostic quality at lower implementation cost.
hypotheses.falsifier: A production compiler benchmark demonstrates equal-or-better rejection, diagnostics and semantic preservation with a fail-open relation grammar.

hypotheses.statement: Executable operator precedence and declarative predicate identity are separate frontend problems and should be represented by separate typed IR layers rather than one overloaded flat operator grammar.
hypotheses.observation: Prior self-conformance work exposed arithmetic/boolean precedence ambiguity while the rule-surface partition independently recovered 17 declarative relations through registered PredicateIR and left three semantic-choice cases.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: One sufficiently rich expression grammar can encode both layers without ambiguity or diagnostic loss.
hypotheses.falsifier: The production BASE parser/type checker expresses all current G9 executable and declarative rules through one grammar with unique ASTs, strong mutation rejection and no semantic escape hatches.
